For the `YYYY-MM-DD` format, as in `2026-10-01`:

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` is the year (four digits).
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` is the month, `01`–`12`.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` is the day, `01`–`31`.
- `^` and `$` make the whole string match. Remove them to find dates inside longer text, and add `\b` at each end if needed.

This checks the format only, not whether the date exists. It still accepts dates like `2026-02-31`. To reject those, parse the matched string with a date library, such as `date.fromisoformat()` in Python.

If you only need the shape and any digits will do, use `^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$`.
